findings.title: Recipient marked by the dative
findings.claim: The second-person dative laka marks the addressee as the person for whom the failed search would matter.
findings.mechanism: The preposition and attached second-person suffix at 17:86:10 specify the recipient/beneficiary relation of tajidu.
findings.reader_payoff: The absence of a wakil is attached to this addressee rather than left as an abstract lack.
findings.containment: Keep the claim local to the dative in 17:86; it does not import a prior-ayah addressee contrast.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC/linguistic support directly grounds the local relation; the claim is confined to 17:86.

findings.title: Recipient becomes exposed seeker
findings.claim: The same singular addressee who received the revelation is now the party for whom no representative can be found.
findings.mechanism: The ila-ka suffix on awhayna and the laka suffix in the later search clause repeat second-person reference across two roles.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus turns the addressee from recipient of the message into the person exposed to its possible removal and unavailable recourse.
findings.containment: The role shift is focus-internal; the proposed link to 17:85 is excluded.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC/linguistic support directly grounds the local relation; the claim is confined to 17:86.

findings.title: Delayed consequence after removal
findings.claim: Thumma places the failed search after the threatened removal rather than alongside it.
findings.mechanism: The connective at 17:86:7 orders the removal clause before la tajidu.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader registers loss first and failed recourse only afterward.
findings.containment: Retain sequencing, not a comparison with the connective at 17:39.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC/linguistic support directly grounds the local relation; the claim is confined to 17:86.

findings.title: Removal turns into attempted recourse
findings.claim: The clause after thumma pivots from what the source could remove to what the addressee could not find.
findings.mechanism: The connective separates dhahabna from the later negative search predicate tajidu.
findings.reader_payoff: The consequence is heard as an aftermath of removal, not as an unrelated second assertion.
findings.containment: This is a local clause relation; the cross-ayah contrast at 17:39 is excluded.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC/linguistic support directly grounds the local relation; the claim is confined to 17:86.

findings.title: Negated finding of a representative
findings.claim: La negates the imperfect tajidu with wakilan as its indefinite object: no representative is available in the stated relation.
findings.mechanism: The negative particle scopes over the finding predicate and its object.
findings.reader_payoff: The clause denies the addressee an available agent, rather than merely reporting that none was named.
findings.containment: Limit the quantificational force to this clause and the wakil role; do not generalize beyond it.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC/linguistic support directly grounds the local relation; the claim is confined to 17:86.

findings.title: Divine agency and human recourse
findings.claim: The focus contrasts first-person divine willing and revealing with the addressee's singular inability to find a wakil.
findings.mechanism: First-person marking on shi'na, awhayna, and alayna frames the acts around second-person address and la tajidu.
findings.reader_payoff: The threatened removal and failed recourse belong to different agency positions in the same utterance.
findings.containment: This is a focus-local grammatical contrast, not a wider doctrine or Surah-wide hierarchy claim.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC/linguistic support directly grounds the local relation; the claim is confined to 17:86.

findings.title: Search survives under negation
findings.claim: The imperfect tajidu preserves the scene of seeking/finding even as la denies its success.
findings.mechanism: Negation takes the imperfect predicate, which still governs the role noun wakilan.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can picture attempted recourse rather than only an abstract proposition of nonexistence.
findings.containment: Do not conflate this processual scene with the categorical scope of the negative clause.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC/linguistic support directly grounds the local relation; the claim is confined to 17:86.

findings.title: Singular capacity and clipped close

findings.title: Wakil as the target of failed recourse

branch_activations.activation: The source-image carrier contacts the conditional and removal consequence without turning the image into an overt direct object.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The source's will can condition the continuing availability of the revealed matter.
branch_activations.boundary: The thing is not an expressed object of shi'na, and the source image is not an independent lexical entailment.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek hareket, bir şeyin bulunduğu yerden gidip ilerlemesi veya geçmesidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The dh-h-b form carries motion away or passing.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Bi and the relative object identify the matter affected by the motion.
branch_activations.activation: Movement away contacts the constructional object in the threatened-removal clause.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The revealed matter can be taken out of the recipient's reach.
branch_activations.boundary: The form does not assert that the removal actually happened.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bilgiyi ya da sözü gizlice iletme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bilgi veya söz bir başkasına gizlilik koşulu altında ulaştırılır.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The named recipient and the separate removal clause delimit the transmission event.
branch_activations.activation: The communicated matter's delivery and possible withdrawal contact across the focus clauses.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The source's conveyance is available to the recipient but is not represented as independently possessed.
branch_activations.boundary: This remains an attributed cross-root model; hidden does not mean unknown to the recipient.

findings.title: Attributed baseline: no counter-custodian
findings.claim: The HFT baseline proposes that no delegate, guarantor, or keeper can establish a claim over the revelation against its source.
findings.mechanism: The failed finding of a wakil contacts delegated representation and custody facets under the negated search and alayna relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing clause denies an effective counter-agent after the revelation's possible removal.
findings.containment: This is an attributed, qualified cross-root model; it does not establish an actual custody event or independently verified HFT provenance.

epistemic.reason: This interpretation is deliberately bounded and preserves alternatives; its local evidence does not justify an unqualified lexical, historical, or doctrinal claim.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bulma ve duyusal ya da zihinsel olarak algılama
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi, özellikle arananı veya yitiği, bulmak ve ona erişmek.
branch_activations.carrier: Tajidu carries the finding/reaching of a sought thing.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: La negates success and wakilan supplies the sought role.
branch_activations.activation: The carrier and denied role connect failed search with unavailable recourse.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: No representative can be found to oppose the source in the stated matter.
branch_activations.boundary: The finding branch does not independently encode custody.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bir işi başkasına devredip onu kendi adına yetkilendirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir işin veya kişinin sorumluluğu, yürütülmesi ya da karara bağlanması için başkasına bırakılır.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Laka marks the relevant interest and alayna marks the opposing party.
branch_activations.activation: The delegated-agent role contacts the focus's explicit against-us relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: No delegate can establish a representative claim against the source.
branch_activations.boundary: The model is interpretive and does not establish a legal proceeding.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenip koruyan yeterli görevli
branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi, kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenir ve onun yürütülmesinden sorumlu olur.
branch_activations.carrier: Wakilan can carry an entrusted keeper's role.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The negative search and alayna delimit the keeper's unavailable function.
branch_activations.activation: Custodial responsibility contacts the denial of any agent against the source.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: No keeper is available to retain or recover the matter against its source.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not entail that the addressee held the revelation as property.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenip koruyan yeterli görevli
branch_activations.facet_statement: Görevli, üstlendiği iş için yeterlilik, koruma ve güvence sağlama işlevlerini taşır.
branch_activations.carrier: The keeper branch can extend to protection and assurance.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The negative search in the alayna relation denies an agent capable of those functions.
branch_activations.activation: The protective extension contacts the same opposed-source constraint.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: No keeper can guarantee the revelation's retention against the source.
branch_activations.boundary: Protection is a branch specialization in the baseline, not an explicit lexical predicate here.
